issues.description: Upsert treats a record as unchanged when only user, partition, submit, start, alloc_cpus, gpus, or exit_code changed, leaving stale accounting data.
Same-rank terminal states overwrite each other without comparing freshness, so an older FAILED/TIMEOUT/etc. snapshot can replace a newer terminal record.
Negative AllocCPUS and gres/gpu values are accepted and can produce negative CPU/GPU-hour reports.
Timezone-aware timestamps are accepted without normalization even though downstream storage and reporting assume comparable timestamp text.
Report filters and MAX compare timestamps lexicographically, which gives wrong results for offset-aware or mixed-format ISO timestamps.
The default database directory and file are created with normal umask permissions, commonly 0755/0644, exposing local job/user data on shared systems.
Report commands call db.connect and silently create a new empty database for a mistyped path instead of failing clearly.
Top users includes zero-GPU pending jobs and can anchor the trailing window on a pending submit time, hiding actual recent GPU usage.
Ingest commits well-formed rows before returning a fatal malformed-row exit code, leaving a nonzero command with persistent partial side effects.
Step detection skips any JobID containing a dot instead of validating Slurm step syntax, risking accidental loss of valid non-step IDs.
Schema has no indexes for reference-time, state, partition, or user report queries, so reports will degrade to full scans as history grows.
Schema has no user_version or migration path, making future active-development changes risky once users have existing databases.
Ingest tests cover lifecycle rank basics but miss changed allocation fields and equal-rank terminal stale-update regressions.
